What if your whole software team was A I? Meet Marina Code Labs, a virtual office in Chennai.
Eight desks, each with one job. CEO, product manager, architect, designer, developers, tester, security officer, and release manager.
Monday, nine A M. A client walks in. Kanchi Silks wants an online store to sell sarees across India.
Step one, the CEO runs office hours. Who will buy? Why online? What is the smallest version worth launching?
Step two, the product manager writes the spec. Catalogue, cart, UPI payment and order tracking. Loyalty points can wait for version two.
Step three, the architect plans the system. A React web app, an API server, a Postgres database, and a payment gateway.
Step four, the designer reviews every screen, from the home page to checkout.
Step five, the developers build it. Frontend, backend and DevOps work side by side, and every change gets a code review.
Step six, the tester places order after order. Empty carts, slow networks, failed payments. Every bug gets logged and fixed.
Step seven, the security officer checks payment safety and customer data.
Step eight, the release manager runs the final tests, merges the code and ships it live.
Friday evening, the team runs a retro. What went well, and what to improve next sprint.
One idea, eight desks, a live store. You are the client. Type the command, and your A I office gets to work.
